relations.definition: Indicates the main entity that the event or claim is about.
relations.embedding_query_text: subject: Indicates the main entity that the event or claim is about.

instances: Fricker performs in Casualty -> Brenda Fricker
Fricker plays Pigeon Lady -> Brenda Fricker

chosen_property.label: mainEntity
chosen_property.justification: Events are about a person; mainEntity fits CreativeWork→Thing, but here Event→Person is acceptable as the primary subject.

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: mainEntityOfPage
candidates.comment: A main entity of page relation between a thing and the creative work or URL for which it is the primary described entity. Also called: primary page, described on page, featured on page. Examples: "Albert Einstein mainEntityOfPage Wikipedia Article", "The Election mainEntityOfPage News Report", "Quantum Physics mainEntityOfPage Research Paper". Distinct from mainEntity, which indicates the primary entity described in a creative work.

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: superEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a smaller event and the larger event of which it is a part. Also called "part of larger event", "parent event", "contained within event", "main event". Examples: "The concert has superEvent the music festival", "The presentation's superEvent is the conference", "This workshop is part of a superEvent summit.". Distinct from subEvent, which points from the larger event to the smaller one.

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

relations.definition: Specifies the date or time when something happened.
relations.embedding_query_text: occurred_on: Specifies the date or time when something happened.

chosen_property.label: timestamp
chosen_property.justification: DeathEvent occurred on a date/time; timestamp fits InstantaneousEvent→DateTime.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

candidates.label: commentTime
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for user comments, indicating the date or date and time when the comment was made. Also called "comment date", "posted time", "submission time". Examples: "User comment commentTime '2023-10-26T10:30:00'", "Review commentTime '2023-09-15'".

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: dateSent
candidates.comment: A temporal dispatch relation between a message and the date/time it was sent. Also called: sending date, message dispatch time, transmission time. Examples: "Email" date sent "2023-10-26T10:20:00Z", "SMS Message" date sent "2023-10-26T10:30:00Z". Distinct from dateReceived, which is when the message arrived.

candidates.label: dateReceived
candidates.comment: A temporal arrival relation between a message and the date/time it was received by the recipient. Also called: reception date, message arrival time, delivery time. Examples: "Email" date received "2023-10-26T10:25:00Z", "Package Notification" date received "2023-10-26T11:00:00Z". Distinct from dateSent, which is when the message was dispatched.

candidates.label: deathDate
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a person and their date of death. Also called: date of demise, passing date, decease date. Examples: "Historical Figure" death date "1963-11-22", "Family Member" death date "2020-05-10". Distinct from birthDate, which is the date of birth.

candidates.label: dateRead
candidates.comment: A temporal interaction relation between a message and the date/time it was read by the recipient. Also called: read date, message read time, recipient read time. Examples: "Email" date read "2023-10-26T10:30:00Z", "Chat Message" date read "2023-10-26T10:35:00Z". Distinct from dateReceived, which is when the message arrived.

relations.definition: Indicates the place where something is situated or occurs.
relations.embedding_query_text: located_in: Indicates the place where something is situated or occurs.

chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: DeathEvent located in a city; location fits Event→Place.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: geoWithin
candidates.comment: A geo within relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is located entirely inside the interior of another containing geometry or place. Also called: is inside, contained in, located within. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo within "Country 'France'", "Office 'Suite 100'" geo within "Building 'Empire State'", "State 'California'" geo within "Country 'USA'". Distinct from geoContains, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

relations.definition: Indicates the reason or factor that leads to an outcome.
relations.embedding_query_text: cause: Indicates the reason or factor that leads to an outcome.

chosen_property.label: cause
chosen_property.justification: DeathEvent caused by a life stage; cause fits MedicalCondition→MedicalCause, but here used broadly for event cause.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: riskFactor
candidates.comment: A factor that increases the likelihood of a patient developing a specific medical condition. Also called predisposing factor, risk element, vulnerability factor. Examples: `Heart Disease` riskFactor `High Cholesterol`, `Diabetes` riskFactor `Obesity`, `Lung Cancer` riskFactor `Smoking`.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: significance
candidates.comment: The medical or diagnostic importance of superficial anatomy, indicating how its characteristics may suggest underlying conditions or treatments. Also called clinical relevance, diagnostic implication, anatomical importance. Examples: `Skin Lesion` significance `"May indicate melanoma"`, `Swollen Lymph Node` significance `"Could suggest infection"`, `Discolored Nail Bed` significance `"Possible circulatory issue"`.

relations.definition: The age of a person when they died.
relations.embedding_query_text: age_at_death: The age of a person when they died.

chosen_property.label: ageAtDeath
chosen_property.definition: The age of a person at the time of their death.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly expresses age at death; minted new property.

candidates.label: deathDate
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a person and their date of death. Also called: date of demise, passing date, decease date. Examples: "Historical Figure" death date "1963-11-22", "Family Member" death date "2020-05-10". Distinct from birthDate, which is the date of birth.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: suggestedAge
candidates.comment: A quantitative value indicating the recommended age or age range for an intended audience or person. Also called "recommended age", "age range", "target age", "suitable age". Examples: "The toy has suggestedAge 3-5 years", "The audience specification includes suggestedAge 18+", "This product is for suggestedAge 6-12 months.". Distinct from suggestedMinAge and suggestedMaxAge, which specify only the minimum or maximum.

candidates.label: requiredMaxAge
candidates.comment: A required maximum age relation between a people audience and the upper age limit for inclusion. Also called max age, age limit. Examples: "A children's event targets a people audience with required max age '12'.", "A youth program has a required max age '25'.", "A senior discount applies to a people audience with required max age '99'."

candidates.label: requiredMinAge
candidates.comment: A required minimum age relation between a people audience and the lower age limit for inclusion. Also called min age, age requirement. Examples: "An adult event targets a people audience with required min age '18'.", "A driving course has a required min age '16'.", "A senior discount applies to a people audience with required min age '65'."

candidates.label: typicalAgeRange
candidates.comment: A typical age range relation between a creative work or event and the expected age group of its audience. Also called age suitability, target age, recommended age. Examples: "Book typicalAgeRange '7-9'", "Movie typicalAgeRange '13+'", "Event typicalAgeRange 'all ages'".

candidates.label: cvdNumC19Died
candidates.comment: A mortality count relation between a CDCPMD record and the number of patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 who died in the hospital, ED, or overflow location. Also called: COVID-19 deaths, C19 fatalities, pandemic deaths. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num c19 died "10", "Facility B Report" cvd num c19 died "3", "Medical Center C" cvd num c19 died "25".

candidates.label: birthDate
candidates.comment: A date representing a person's birth. Also called: date of birth, birthday. Examples: "Person 'John Doe' birthDate '1980-05-15'", "Person 'Jane Smith' birthDate '1992-11-22'."

candidates.label: suggestedMaxAge
candidates.comment: A numerical value indicating the maximum recommended age in years for an audience or user. Also called "maximum age", "upper age limit", "age cap". Examples: "The game has suggestedMaxAge 12", "The audience specification includes suggestedMaxAge 65", "This content is suitable up to suggestedMaxAge 18.". Distinct from suggestedAge, which specifies a range, and suggestedMinAge, which specifies only the minimum.

candidates.label: yearsInOperation
candidates.comment: An operational age relation between a business audience and a quantitative value, indicating the number of years the business has been active. Also called business age, operational duration, years active. Examples: TargetAudience yearsInOperation "5-10 years", BusinessAudience yearsInOperation "over 20 years", StartupAudience yearsInOperation "under 2 years".

relations.definition: Indicates the person or entity that verified or affirmed something.
relations.embedding_query_text: confirmed_by: Indicates the person or entity that verified or affirmed something.

chosen_property.label: recognizedBy
chosen_property.justification: DeathEvent confirmed by a person; recognizedBy fits Credential→Organization, but here used for confirmation by a person.

candidates.label: verificationFactCheckingPolicy
candidates.comment: A verification fact-checking policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a disclosure about its verification and fact-checking processes. Also called fact-checking policy, verification standards, editorial policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization verificationFactCheckingPolicy 'https://example.com/fact-check-policy'", "Organization verificationFactCheckingPolicy 'Our journalists verify all claims.'", "News outlet verificationFactCheckingPolicy 'https://example.com/editorial-standards'".

candidates.label: confirmationNumber
candidates.comment: An identification relation for an invoice or order, providing a number that confirms its receipt. Also called "order confirmation", "booking reference", "receipt number". Examples: "Online order confirmationNumber 'ABC-12345'", "Flight invoice confirmationNumber 'XYZ-67890'".

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: recognizedBy
candidates.comment: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."

candidates.label: reservationStatus
candidates.comment: A reservation status relation between a reservation and its current state, such as confirmed or cancelled. Also called booking status, status of reservation. Examples: "A flight reservation has a reservation status 'Confirmed'.", "A hotel booking has a reservation status 'Pending'.", "A restaurant reservation has a reservation status 'Cancelled'."

candidates.label: recognizingAuthority
candidates.comment: A recognizing authority relation between a medical entity and the organization that officially endorses it within a system of medicine. Also called endorsed by, officially recognized by. Examples: "A medical treatment is recognized by 'the World Health Organization'.", "A medical specialty is recognized by 'the American Medical Association'.", "A traditional medicine practice is recognized by 'a national health ministry'."

candidates.label: legislationCountersignedBy
candidates.comment: A countersignature relation between a piece of legislation and the person or organization that countersigned it. Also called: countersigned by, officially endorsed by, co-signed by. Examples: "The Bill of Rights legislationCountersignedBy President Washington", "EU Directive 2023/45 legislationCountersignedBy European Commission", "Local Ordinance legislationCountersignedBy City Clerk".

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: certificationStatus
candidates.comment: A status relation for a certification, indicating whether it is active or inactive. Also called "certificate status", "certification validity", "status of certification". Examples: "Product certification certificationStatus Active", "Company certification certificationStatus Inactive".

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

relations.definition: Indicates the source that reported the information.
relations.embedding_query_text: reported_by: Indicates the source that reported the information.

chosen_property.label: source
chosen_property.justification: DeathEvent reported by a news organization; source fits InstantaneousEvent→Thing.

candidates.label: reportNumber
candidates.comment: A report number relation between a report and the unique identifier assigned by its publisher. Also called report ID, document number. Examples: "A financial report has a report number 'FY2023-Q4'.", "A technical report has a report number 'TR-001-2024'.", "A government report has a report number 'GAO-24-123'."

candidates.label: dateline
candidates.comment: A textual origin relation between a news article and the brief text describing where and when the story was written or filed. Also called: news origin, article origin, reporting location. Examples: "News Report" dateline "BEIRUT, Lebanon, June 2.", "Article" dateline "Paris, France", "Dispatch" dateline "December 19, 2017 11:43AM Reporting from Washington". Distinct from locationCreated, which is a structured representation of the creation location.

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: healthcareReportingData
candidates.comment: A healthcare reporting data relation between a hospital and its associated reporting data, such as CDC records or datasets. Also called hospital data, reporting dataset, healthcare metrics. Examples: "A hospital has healthcare reporting data from the CDC.", "The hospital provides healthcare reporting data as a dataset.", "This facility publishes its healthcare reporting data."

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: printSection
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the specific print section where a news article appeared. Also called section name, newspaper section, print category. Examples: A news article appears in print section 'Sports'. The story is in print section 'Business'. The article's print section is 'Opinion'.

candidates.label: citation
candidates.comment: A reference relation between a creative work and another creative work or text that it cites. Also called "reference", "cited work", "source". Examples: "Research paper citation 'Smith, J. (2020). Article Title.'", "Blog post citation 'https://example.com/article'".

candidates.label: unnamedSourcesPolicy
candidates.comment: An unnamed sources policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a statement about its policy on using unnamed sources. Also called anonymous sources policy, source confidentiality policy, disclosure policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/sources-policy'", "Organization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'Our policy requires two independent sources.'", "News outlet unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/ethics'".

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

relations.definition: The date on which something was publicly declared.
relations.embedding_query_text: announced_on: The date on which something was publicly declared.

chosen_property.label: datePublished
chosen_property.justification: DeathEvent announced on a day; datePublished fits CreativeWork→Date, but here used for event announcement date.

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: dateCreated
candidates.comment: A temporal origin relation between a creative work or data feed item and the date it was created or added. Also called: creation date, date of origin, initial date. Examples: "Painting" date created "1889-05-01", "Blog Post" date created "2023-03-15T10:00:00Z", "Data Feed Entry" date created "2023-01-01". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first public release.

candidates.label: datePosted
candidates.comment: A temporal publication relation between a CDCPMD record, job posting, real estate listing, or special announcement and its online publication date. Also called: posting date, publication date, listing date. Examples: "Job Opening" date posted "2023-10-25", "Apartment for Rent" date posted "2023-10-20", "Public Health Alert" date posted "2023-03-01T09:00:00Z". Distinct from datePublished, which is a more general property for first publication.

candidates.label: purchaseDate
candidates.comment: A purchase date relation between a product or vehicle and the date it was acquired by its current owner. Also called acquired on, bought on, ownership date. Examples: "A car has a purchase date of 2020-05-10.", "A smartphone has a purchase date of 2023-01-15.", "A house has a purchase date of 2018-07-22.". Distinct from productionDate, which is the date the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: datePublished
candidates.comment: A temporal release relation between a certification or creative work and its date of first publication or broadcast. Also called: publication date, broadcast date, release date. Examples: "Book" date published "1984-06-08", "TV Show Episode" date published "2023-01-01", "Certification" date published "2022-12-01". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the date of creation, and datePosted, which is for online listings.

candidates.label: legislationDate
candidates.comment: A date relation between a piece of legislation and its official adoption or signature date. Also called: date of adoption, signature date, enactment date. Examples: "The Civil Rights Act legislationDate 1964-07-02", "GDPR legislationDate 2016-04-27", "Local Bylaw legislationDate 2023-01-15".

candidates.label: dateVehicleFirstRegistered
candidates.comment: A temporal registration relation between a vehicle and the date of its first registration with public authorities. Also called: first registration date, initial registration, vehicle registration date. Examples: "A movie's actors include 'Brad Pitt'.", "An episode's actors include 'Jennifer Aniston'." Distinct from actor, which is the preferred and more general property that also allows PerformingGroup.

candidates.label: children
candidates.comment: A familial relation between a person and their child. Also called "offspring", "son", "daughter". Examples: "John children Jane", "Mary children Peter". Distinct from parent, which indicates the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: characterAttribute
candidates.comment: An attribute relation describing a particular aspect of a fictional character within a game or video game series. Also called "character trait", "character property", "game attribute". Examples: "Video game character attribute 'Strength'", "RPG game character attribute 'Magic Resistance'".

candidates.label: roleName
candidates.comment: The specific designation or title of a role performed by a person or organization. Also called role title, position name, function name. Examples: `Person in Movie` roleName `"Actor"`, `Team Member` roleName `"Quarterback"`, `Project Contributor` roleName `"Lead Developer"`.

candidates.label: sibling
candidates.comment: A familial relationship between two people who share at least one parent. Also called brother, sister, kin, family member. Examples: `John Doe` sibling `Jane Doe`, `Mary Smith` sibling `Tom Smith`, `Alice Brown` sibling `Bob Brown`. Distinct from `siblings`, which is the plural form.

relations.definition: Received a prize or honor.
relations.embedding_query_text: won_award: Received a prize or honor.

chosen_property.label: award
chosen_property.justification: Person won an award; award fits Person→Text, but here used for Person→Event.

candidates.label: award
candidates.comment: An award won by or for a creative work, organization, person, product, or service. Also called: honor, prize, recognition. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' award 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' award 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' award 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from awards, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: awards
candidates.comment: Awards won by or for a creative work, organization, person, or product. Also called: honors, prizes, recognitions. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' awards 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' awards 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' awards 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from award, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: educationalCredentialAwarded
candidates.comment: An educational credential awarded relation between a course or program and the credential received upon successful completion. Also called "award received", "qualification granted", "certificate earned". Examples: "Course 'Introduction to Python' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Certificate of Completion'", "Program 'MBA' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Master of Business Administration'", "Training 'First Aid' educationalCredentialAwarded 'First Aid Certification'".

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: occupationalCredentialAwarded
candidates.comment: An occupational credential, such as a qualification, award, certificate, or diploma, awarded upon successful completion of a course or program. Also called credential earned, qualification awarded, program certification. Examples: "Course X occupationalCredentialAwarded 'Certificate of Completion'", "Program Y occupationalCredentialAwarded 'Bachelor of Science'", "Training Z occupationalCredentialAwarded 'Professional Certification'". Distinct from educationalLevel, which describes the level of education attained.

candidates.label: honorificPrefix
candidates.comment: An honorific prefix relation between a person and a title preceding their name. Also called title, salutation, courtesy title. Examples: "A person has an honorific prefix 'Dr.'.", "Her honorific prefix is 'Ms.'.", "The individual uses the honorific prefix 'Mr.'."

candidates.label: honorificSuffix
candidates.comment: An honorific suffix relation between a person and a title following their name. Also called post-nominal title, suffix title, academic suffix. Examples: "A person has an honorific suffix 'PhD'.", "His honorific suffix is 'M.D.'.", "The individual uses the honorific suffix 'Jr.'."

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

candidates.label: candidate
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a vote action, indicating the person who is being voted for. Also called "voted for", "nominee", "electoral candidate". Examples: "Election vote action candidate Jane Smith", "Award vote action candidate John Doe".

candidates.label: fundedItem
candidates.comment: A funded item relation between a grant and the biochemical entity, creative work, event, medical entity, organization, person, or product that receives direct or indirect funding or sponsorship. Also called: grant recipient, sponsored item, supported entity. Examples: "Research Grant" funded item "Cancer Research Project", "Arts Grant" funded item "Local Theater Production", "Educational Grant" funded item "Student Scholarship Program". Distinct from funding, which is the grant itself.

relations.definition: Authored or composed a work.
relations.embedding_query_text: wrote: Authored or composed a work.

instances: Brenda Fricker -> She Died Young: A Life in Fragments

chosen_property.label: author
chosen_property.justification: Person wrote a book; author fits CreativeWork→Person, but here used as Person→Book (inverse direction).

candidates.label: composer
candidates.comment: A creative role relation between an event or music composition and the organization or person who wrote it. Also called "writer", "creator", "author of music". Examples: "Symphony music composition composer Ludwig van Beethoven", "Concert event composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart". Distinct from byArtist, which is the performer of a musical work.

candidates.label: author
candidates.comment: An organization or person who created content or a rating. Also called: creator, writer, originator, composer. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Novel' author 'Jane Austen'", "Rating 'Product Review' author 'Consumer Reports'", "CreativeWork 'Article' author 'New York Times'". Distinct from artist, which is typically for visual or comic art.

candidates.label: lyricist
candidates.comment: A lyricist relation between a music composition and the person who wrote its words. Also called: songwriter, words by, author of lyrics. Examples: "Bohemian Rhapsody lyricist Freddie Mercury", "Yesterday lyricist Paul McCartney", "Hallelujah lyricist Leonard Cohen".

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: material
candidates.comment: A material composition relation between a creative work or product and the material it is made from. Also called: made of, composed of, constructed from. Examples: "Wooden Chair material Wood", "Wool Sweater material Wool", "Paper Book material Paper".

candidates.label: text
candidates.comment: The primary textual content of a creative work. Also called "content text", "body text", "written content", "main text". Examples: "The article has text 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet...'", "The book's text is its full narrative", "This creative work's text is its script."

candidates.label: musicBy
candidates.comment: A composer or music group responsible for the soundtrack of a creative work. Also called soundtrack by, composer of, musical score by. Examples: "Movie X musicBy 'John Williams'", "TV Series Y musicBy 'Ramin Djawadi'", "Video Game Z musicBy 'Koji Kondo'". Distinct from composer, which is for the composer of a MusicComposition.

candidates.label: lyrics
candidates.comment: A lyrics relation between a music composition and the creative work containing its words. Also called: song words, text of song, musical text. Examples: "Bohemian Rhapsody lyrics 'Is this the real life? Is this just fantasy?'", "Yesterday lyrics 'Yesterday, all my troubles seemed so far away'", "Hallelujah lyrics 'I've heard there was a secret chord'".

candidates.label: editor
candidates.comment: An editor relation between a creative work and the person who edited it. Also called "edited by", "compiled by", "prepared by". Examples: "Book 'The Great Gatsby' editor 'Maxwell Perkins'", "Journal article editor 'Dr. Jane Doe'", "Film 'Pulp Fiction' editor 'Sally Menke'".

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

relations.definition: The duration of time spent writing something.
relations.embedding_query_text: took_years_to_write: The duration of time spent writing something.

chosen_property.label: timeRequired
chosen_property.justification: Person took years to write; timeRequired fits CreativeWork→Duration, but here used for Person→Duration.

candidates.label: timeRequired
candidates.comment: A duration representing the approximate time typically needed for an audience to engage with or complete a creative work. Also called "completion time", "estimated duration", "reading time", "viewing time". Examples: "The article has timeRequired 10 minutes", "The course's timeRequired is 40 hours", "This creative work takes timeRequired 2 hours to watch."

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: timeToComplete
candidates.comment: A duration representing the expected length of time to complete an educational or occupational program when attending full-time. Also called "program duration", "completion duration", "full-time study length", "expected completion time". Examples: "The degree program has timeToComplete 4 years", "The certification's timeToComplete is 6 months", "This program requires timeToComplete 2 years of full-time study."

candidates.label: loanTerm
candidates.comment: A loan duration relation between a loan or credit and the quantitative value representing its agreement term. Also called: loan duration, credit term, repayment period. Examples: "Car Loan loanTerm '60 months'", "Mortgage loanTerm '30 years'", "Personal Loan loanTerm '5 years'".

candidates.label: yearsInOperation
candidates.comment: An operational age relation between a business audience and a quantitative value, indicating the number of years the business has been active. Also called business age, operational duration, years active. Examples: TargetAudience yearsInOperation "5-10 years", BusinessAudience yearsInOperation "over 20 years", StartupAudience yearsInOperation "under 2 years".

candidates.label: totalTime
candidates.comment: A total time relation between instructions or a direction and the overall duration required to perform them, including preparation. Also called overall duration, completion time, estimated time. Examples: "HowTo totalTime 'PT2H30M'", "HowToDirection totalTime 'PT15M'", "Recipe totalTime 'PT1H'".

candidates.label: temporalCoverage
candidates.comment: A temporal scope relation between a creative work and the specific time period that its content describes or applies to. Also called "time period covered", "content timeframe", "temporal scope", "date range of content". Examples: "A census dataset has temporalCoverage 2011/2012", "The historical novel's temporalCoverage is 1939/1945", "This research paper's temporalCoverage is 2015-11/..". Distinct from temporal, which is a more general temporal association when the specific scope is not known.

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: termDuration
candidates.comment: A duration representing the length of a term of study within an educational or occupational program. Also called "term length", "semester duration", "quarter length", "study period duration". Examples: "The program has termDuration 15 weeks", "The educational program's termDuration is 10 weeks", "This course has a termDuration of one semester."

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

relations.definition: Had the ability to use or manage a body part.
relations.embedding_query_text: had_control_of: Had the ability to use or manage a body part.

chosen_property.label: nerveMotor
chosen_property.justification: Person had control of a body part; nerveMotor fits Nerve→Muscle, but here used for Person→AnatomicalStructure.

candidates.label: nerveMotor
candidates.comment: A muscle controlled by a nerve through a neurological pathway. Also called motor innervation, controls muscle, innervates muscle. Examples: "Radial Nerve nerveMotor 'Triceps Brachii'", "Musculocutaneous Nerve nerveMotor 'Biceps Brachii'", "Phrenic Nerve nerveMotor 'Diaphragm'". Distinct from nerve, which describes the nerve of a muscle.

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: skills
candidates.comment: The competencies, knowledge, or abilities possessed by a person or organization, or required for a job or occupation. Also called competencies, abilities, qualifications, expertise. Examples: `Job Posting: Software Engineer` skills `"Python, Java, SQL"`, `Person: Jane Doe` skills `"Project Management, Public Speaking"`, `Occupation: Doctor` skills `"Diagnosis, Patient Care"`. Distinct from `qualifications`, which are formal requirements.

candidates.label: physicalRequirement
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute detailing the physical activities or abilities required for a job posting. Also called physical demands, fitness requirements, job physicality. Examples: A job posting has a physical requirement of 'ability to lift 50 lbs'. A job posting has a physical requirement of 'standing for long periods'. A job posting has a physical requirement of 'manual dexterity'.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: accessibilityControl
candidates.comment: An accessibility control relation between a creative work and the input methods sufficient for its full control. Also called control methods, input compatibility, interaction modes. Examples: "A video game's accessibility control is 'keyboard'.", "A web application's accessibility control is 'mouse'."

candidates.label: bodyLocation
candidates.comment: A textual description of the location in the body of an anatomical structure or for a medical procedure. Also called: anatomical site, body region, procedure location. Examples: "AnatomicalStructure 'Heart' bodyLocation 'Chest'", "MedicalProcedure 'Appendectomy' bodyLocation 'Abdomen'."

candidates.label: legalStatus
candidates.comment: A regulatory status relation between a dietary supplement, drug, or medical entity and its legal classification, including controlled substance schedules. Also called regulatory status, legal classification, controlled substance status, drug schedule. Examples: A drug has a legalStatus of 'PrescriptionOnly'. A dietary supplement has a legalStatus of 'OverTheCounter'. A medication has a legalStatus of 'Schedule II controlled substance'. Distinct from drugClass, which is a medical classification, not a legal one.

candidates.label: permittedUsage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."
